Hi Samantha — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. Sorry you're seeing that.

Quick diagnostic notes:
- When an invite is forwarded, some calendar clients rebuild the event and can inject a new join token/shortlink; that can produce an entry with a different token that doesn't map to the original host claim.
- If a guest accepts an invite that has a different join token, Meet/SSO may block them because they're not in the same token lineage.

Plan (short):
1) Ben/LA will regenerate a fresh invite from our demo account and send as a *new* calendar event (not a forwarded update).
2) We'll include an alternate Zoom link as a fallback (passcode + shortlink) and mark it in the event body clearly.
3) Ask you and your ops team to delete any duplicate calendar entries and accept only the new invite.

Can you confirm you can delete the forwarded copy on your side? Also please share any guest orgs that enforce SSO (we may need to pre-provision a guest pass).

I'll loop Ben and Lauren for the resend.

— Ava
